title: TATOO: A Flexible Hardware Platform for Binary-Only Fuzzing
problem: Hardware-based tracing lacks flexibility to re-filter branches recorded in specified address ranges, limiting efficiency. Software-based instrumentation for binary-only fuzzing is computationally expensive.
motivation: Reducing computational overhead and improving flexibility in binary-only fuzzing accelerates vulnerability detection and strengthens software security testing.
method: Tatoo attaches metadata tags to each instruction as the CPU executes them, allowing the hardware to selectively record which instructions' data to trace (rather than recording everything). By capturing just the dataflow information—which data flows through which instructions—it provides the fuzzer with enough detail to make intelligent mutations (changes to test inputs). The system runs on an FPGA and adds 8.7% performance overhead.
key_novelty: The innovation is using tagged architectures—CPU designs where each instruction carries metadata—to enable flexible, fine-grained filtering of hardware traces during fuzzing.
contributions: Instruction-level tagging mechanism for flexible trace filtering
Hardware-accelerated binary fuzzing platform using tagged architectures
FPGA implementation with low performance overhead (8.7%)
